article.title: Explainer-What has turned the Afghan Taliban and Pakistan from partners to foes?
article.summary: By Asif ShahzadISLAMABAD, Sept 24 (Reuters) - Pakistan's air force struck 10 locations in Afghanistan on Thursday, its second round of strikes in four days after three months of relative quiet along the two countries' 2,600-km (1,600-mile) border.Islamabad said it struck militant hideouts in retaliation for drones launched from Afghanistan. Kabul denied sending the drones and said the seven Afghan fatalities in strikes this week were all civilians.Here is what is driving the latest escalation, and why previous attempts to contain it have failed.

article.title: Pakistan Airstrikes On Afghanistan: Taliban Clash Escalates | Shehbaz Sharif At UNGA | News18
article.summary: Pakistan-Afghanistan tensions have intensified after Islamabad said it carried out precision aerial and drone strikes at 10 locations in Afghanistan, describing them as sites used to launch and store drones. Pakistan has also reported a fresh clash with Afghan Taliban forces in the Gulistan sector.The escalation comes as Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif attends the 81st UN General Assembly in New York. Sharif is expected to address regional security and terrorism, while tensions with Afghanistan remain a key concern.Afghanistan has condemned Pakistani military action, while UN reporting has documented civilian casualties from earlier Pakistani strikes. article.title: At UN, Pakistan PM Says Afghan Territory Is Being Used for Attacks Against Pakistan
article.summary: KABUL, AFGHANISTAN - Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has raised the situation in Afghanistan under Taliban control during his address to the United Nations General Assembly, accusing militant groups of using Afghan territory to carry out attacks in Pakistan while also calling for the protection of Afghans’ fundamental rights, particularly those of women and girls.Sharif said the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) were using Afghan territory to conduct attacks inside Pakistan. He called on the Taliban authorities to fulfill their international commitments and take “verifiable” measures to prevent Afghan soil from being used against Pakistan or any other country.The postAt UN, Pakistan PM Says Afghan Territory Is Being Used for Attacks Against Pakistanappeared first onKabulNow.
